question.problem: Find the disjoint union of the sets ${A}_{1}=\{a,b,c\}$ and ${A}_{2}=\{b,c,d\}.$
question.worked_solution:
Notice that the sets are overlapping since

$$
\{a,b,c\}\cap \{b,c,d\}=\{b,c\}\ne ∅.
$$

So, for each of our sets, we form the associated set, where each element is tagged with the corresponding index, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned} & {A}_{1} &  & \,\to \, &  & {A}_{1}^{∗}=\{(a,1),(b,1),(c,1)\} \\  & {A}_{2} &  & \,\to \, &  & {A}_{2}^{∗}=\{(b,2),(c,2),(d,2)\}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the disjoint union of our sets is simply the union of the associated tagged sets:

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{1}⊔{A}_{2} & =\{a,b,c\}⊔\{b,c,d\} \\  & ={A}_{1}^{∗}\cup {A}_{2}^{∗} \\  & =\{(a,1),(b,1),(c,1)\}\cup \{(b,2),(c,2),(d,2)\} \\  & =\{(a,1),(b,1),(c,1),(b,2),(c,2),(d,2)\}\end{aligned}
$$
